cases.claim_scope: INTEGRATION study on a DIFFERENT laminate from id 05: a probe-fed 40x50 mm patch on RT/Duroid 5880 (eps_r 2.2, h = 3.175 mm) built identically in rfx and openEMS on a UNIFORM dx = h/4 = 793.75 um mesh (no dz_profile, so the #325 graded-mesh class cannot arise; the script asserts the substrate rasterizes to exactly 4 z-cells before quoting any f0). It exercises probe/lumped feed + finite ground plane + CPML + ring-down harminv + NTFF directivity end-to-end and gates a same-geometry coarse-mesh envelope: rfx ring-down f0 vs the openEMS S11 dip within 8%, the -40 dB open-domain settling witness, passivity on BOTH legs (max|S11| <= 1.05), and broadside directivity within 3 dB. Patch ACCURACY is NOT claimed here and is NOT re-opened: it remains DELEGATED to the committed tests, which stay authoritative -- gated primarily by `tests/crossval/test_patch_canonical_farfield_e4.py`, with `tests/crossval/test_patch_msl_public_carriers.py`, `tests/crossval/test_lattice_ownership_crossval_witness.py`, `tests/locks/test_patch_edgefed_resonance_harminv.py` and `tests/contracts/test_evidence_citation_pointers.py` also reading the same fixture. That fixture, `tests/fixtures/patch_canonical_farfield_e4/patch_farfield_openems.json`, carries its own `meta.reproduce_gate` record of openEMS's canonical Simple_Patch_Antenna tutorial reproduction; its supporting VESSL reverify logs (runs 369367247470 and 369367247478) are TRACKED as of 2026-09-10 at `tests/fixtures/patch_canonical_farfield_e4/canonical_nf2ff_reverify_369367247470_completed.log` and `tests/fixtures/patch_canonical_farfield_e4/canonical_nf2ff_reverify_369367247478_completed.log` -- moved out of the gitignored `docs/research_notes/vessl_logs/`, the same fix the coax thru-line case's REPRODUCE_GATE_RECORD history already made for the identical reason -- so a reviewer outside this machine can now open the log a claimed number came from. id 05 (05_patch_antenna) is retired from the scheduled crossval cases as of 2026-09-10 (docs/design_notes/20260910_cv05_crossval_disposition.md), its script file retained, unscheduled. MERGE OF TWO INDEPENDENT FIXES (2026-09-10): main issue #920 (the rfx probe post floated between the two conductors, touching neither -- closes #920) and this branch's issue #931 (the lattice ownership contract: BOTH conductors declared SHEETS -- zero-thickness PEC `Box`es on the two substrate faces, the same structure both openEMS legs build; before #931 the ground was a one-cell PEC Box drawn below the floor and flagged `two_plane=True` (issue #706) so a second wall landed on z_sub_lo, and #931 deletes the flag along with the volume declaration it patched). These are NOT two compounding changes: #920's derivation (the port spans from the ground Box's realized corner to the patch Box's) and #931's independently-chosen full-substrate feed (`z_sub_lo -> z_sub_hi`) are algebraically the SAME span once both conductors are sheets, because a sheet's `corner_lo` and `corner_hi` coincide -- verified by measurement, not assumed: the merged code reproduces the pre-merge #931 leg's settling witness bit-for-bit (-68.69142333390357 dB). `assert_galvanic_feed`/`_feed_check_ok` (#920) had to be RESPELT for sheets: a sheet's normal E component never goes PEC (design note §1.3, "normal E through a sheet stays live"), so #920's original first/last-cell-dead criterion is unsatisfiable on this board and was replaced with a plane criterion -- the feed's two endpoints must themselves be realized conductor wall planes, read through the SAME `realized_pec_edge_masks`/`realized_wall_planes` pair `assert_realized_stack` uses. `assert_realized_stack()` reads the contract's one edge set and refuses to quote f0 unless the realized wall planes over the patch footprint are EXACTLY {z_sub_lo, z_sub_hi} -- no wall at k_patch+1 -- and the assembled eps_r still holds exactly the two declared values, a sheet owning no cell and writing no material. MEASURED on the merged leg (VESSL 369367260032): rfx reads 3.99 % HIGH vs openEMS (2.4230 vs 2.330 GHz) and +0.31 % vs the analytic anchor, openEMS -3.54 %. The two solvers no longer sit on the same side of the closed form -- rfx reads high, openEMS low -- and the rfx-vs-openEMS distance grew from 0.69 % to 3.99 % while the rfx-vs-analytic distance shrank from -4.21 % to +0.31 %; the openEMS leg did not move. The S11 dip deepened from -4.4 dB to -19.0 dB against openEMS's -20.1 dB, off-resonance max|S11| went from 0.787 to 0.991 against openEMS's 0.992, and the ring-down Q fell from 18.9 to 10.1: the feed now reaches the conductor instead of coupling capacitively. A decomposition run on the pre-merge #931-only base (production sheets with the PRE-#931 feed, VESSL 369367259279, `_15_patch_results/rfx_decomposition_feed_pre931.json`) splits the +4.71 % into 58 % / 42 % -- from the #768 leg to sheets with the pre-#931 feed is +2.74 % (2.3139 → 2.3774 GHz, Q 18.9 → 18.3), and from there to the full-span feed a further +1.92 % (2.3774 → 2.4230 GHz, Q 18.3 → 10.1, and essentially all of the Q collapse). Only the second step is a clean A/B: both its legs are on one code state and differ only in the declared feed span. UNEXPLAINED REMAINDER (2026-09-10): a further isolating leg (VESSL 369367260082, `validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/rfx_decomposition_patchkind_volume_1cell.json`) measured the patch-declaration term alone (volume -> sheet, ground and feed held at their current values) at +111.827 MHz (+4.838 %) -- larger than the +2.74 % (63.484 MHz) first-step bundle it sits inside. The ground-declaration term (two_plane -> sheet) is not isolated by any leg in this record. The terms do not sum, by an amount and sign this record does not explain; nobody has measured the ground leg alone. The old 0.69 % agreement with openEMS was therefore not a better model: it was a cavity electrically 55 % too thick, read through a feed that never touched the patch. Both pre-fix legs are preserved verbatim: `validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/rfx_pre931_two_plane_ground_1f005d0d.json` (this branch's archival name) and `validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/rfx_floating_post_1f005d0d.json` (main's archival name for the SAME bytes, sha256 identical -- both kept because each has its own dated documents citing it; see the branch-merge resolution note). All seven gates pass on the merged leg, including the stack gate and the respelt galvanic-feed gate. ISSUE #812 (2026-09-01, round 2): the f0 gate is BLIND to the #740 one-plane-ground realization that PR #768 fixed -- the pre-fix leg reads `validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/rfx_one_plane_ground_b29f9de7.json::f_harminv_hz = 2471858108` Hz against the openEMS dip `validation/crossval/_15_patch_results/openems.json::f_dip_hz = 2330000000` Hz, +6.09 %, inside the 8 % gate, and only assert_realized_stack (a build assertion, not a physics gate) catches it. A mode-pair RATIO gate was tried: a declared-anchored band CAN separate the two builds (the admissible half-width interval is `tests/fixtures/patch_mode_identification/cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json::declared_anchored_band.admissible_interval_is_nonempty`, from `tests/fixtures/patch_mode_identification/cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json::declared_anchored_band.min_half_width_admitting_correct_build = 0.001407` to `tests/fixtures/patch_mode_identification/cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json::declared_anchored_band.max_half_width_still_rejecting_740 = 0.003338`), but both endpoints are properties of the two measurements the band would judge and the interval is `tests/fixtures/patch_mode_identification/cv15_mode_pair_ratio_band.json::declared_anchored_band.upper_endpoint_over_identification_tolerance = 0.0314` of the tightest window derivable from geometry alone, so no window with provenance this lane can supply meets criterion (B). cv15 is an honest STOP: no re-gate, script and committed leg unchanged, the blindness stated here.
